title: Sleep Underpins the Plasticity of Language Production

selection.evidence: Assigned by mark as item 4 of 8 in a blinded known-answer control of my reading protocol (identifiers only, 2026-10-23T16:11). No prior knowledge of the paper; prior suspicion: none.

cost.compute_notes: Accepted manuscript + supplement (White Rose eprint 79436) read in full; the Hull 'Supplemental_information.pdf' link returned an HTML page. OSF zqg9y holds no files itself; 5 components acquired with checksums. Authors' two lme4 scripts run in Docker zoo-r-psych:4.4.1 (lme4 1.1-35.5) with a stringsAsFactors shim; maximal glmer models are slow and several fail to converge. Python: Table 1-3 recounts, cluster-robust and full-term GLMs, participant-level ANCOVA, 100k-permutation test, split-half reliability.

claims.statement: Speech errors after a 90-min nap, but not after equivalent wake, come to respect newly experienced second-order phonotactic constraints: Group x Session x Restriction beta = 1.97, SE = .50, z = 3.31, p < .001.
claims.scope: N = 38 (19 nap, 19 wake), 5,084 coded speech errors; mixed logistic regression with maximal random slopes.

quantities.name: three_way_interaction_beta_current_lme4
quantities.baseline: SE 0.59965, z 3.269, p 0.00108 (published SE .50, z 3.31); model fails to converge in 10,000 evaluations

quantities.name: phonotactic_score_change_sleep_pts
quantities.baseline: wake -5.53; sleep vs wake change t = 2.76, p = 0.0089; permutation p = 0.008

quantities.name: ancova_sleep_minus_wake_at_test_adjusting_training
quantities.baseline: p = 0.039; training-score slope 0.047; baseline imbalance wake +8.79 vs sleep -2.03 (t = -1.78, p = 0.083)

our_assessment.why: Point estimate reproduces exactly. But the groups differed at baseline by chance in opposite directions and the training score does not predict the test score (slope .05), so the change-score interaction is inflated by regression to the mean. ANCOVA keeps a sleep advantage of 9.2 points at p = .039, not p < .001. The post-hoc 'matched subset' (28 of 38 chosen by excluding on the baseline score) is the unprincipled version of the same correction; its follow-up tests become non-significant in current lme4 (p .021 -> .085, .017 -> .105).

claims.statement: Only the nap group generalised the constraints to new syllables: sleep 69% vs wake 56% correct, Group beta = 1.11, SE = .53, z = 2.08, p = .038; both-unfamiliar items above chance for sleep (z = 2.59, p = .0096) but not wake (p = .54).
claims.scope: 2AFC generalisation, 37 participants (one wake participant's test data lost), 19-20 trials each.

quantities.name: gen_raw_accuracy_sleep_pct
quantities.baseline: wake 54.3; the published 69/56 is the unweighted mean of three item-type means (68.7/56.1)

quantities.name: gen_group_beta_current_lme4
quantities.baseline: SE 0.47596, z 2.326, p 0.020 (published SE .53, z 2.08, p .038); model fails to converge

our_assessment.why: The group effect is tested and reproduces (p = .020 to .038 depending on lme4 version). 'Only the sleep group generalised' rests on a significant vs non-significant comparison with chance; the group x type interactions are null. Table 2's '(SD)' are standard errors (recomputed SEs match the print; true SDs 16-31%).

claims.statement: The speech-error shift in the nap group is associated with slow-wave sleep: Session x Restriction x SWS duration beta = 0.06, SE = .02, z = 3.10, p = .002 (r = .47), corroborated by delta power (beta = 0.006, z = 2.64, p = .008).
claims.scope: Sleep group only, n = 19 participants, 2,401 speech errors.

quantities.name: sws_glm_published_formula_z
quantities.baseline: glm with no participant term and no lower-order terms -- the authors' own formula, reproduced exactly

quantities.name: sws_participant_level_r
quantities.baseline: p = 0.044 (permutation 0.046); REM r = -0.494; delta power r = 0.397, p = 0.093; 6 sleep measures, no correction

our_assessment.why: The published z = 3.10 comes from a logistic regression over speech errors as if they were independent participants, without lower-order terms. With participants as clusters and a proper model it is p = .057; at the participant level r = .47, p = .044, one of six uncorrected sleep measures, matched by an opposite REM correlation. Delta power, offered as converging evidence, is p = .09 at the participant level.

claims.statement: Table 1's standard deviations are rotated by one block in every column: the SD printed for training belongs to test block 1, the one printed for test 1 belongs to test 2, and the one printed for test 2 belongs to training (e.g. sleep/restricted error counts printed 9.5 (4.7), 4.9 (3.8), 6.0 (5.4); true 9.5 (5.4), 4.9 (4.7), 6.0 (3.8)). Means are correct and are pooled over errors, while the SDs are across participants.
claims.scope: Table 1, all 8 columns (group x restriction, percentage and count rows).

our_assessment.why: Recomputed from the deposited error-level data; the rotation is consistent across all 24 printed SDs.

checked.result: 38 participants (19/19), all with all 3 blocks (the paper says one participant's speech errors were excluded; the file has 38). Covariates are centred; participant-level variables repeated on each error row.

checked.how: docker run zoo-r-psych:4.4.1 Rscript -e 'read.csv <- function(...) utils::read.csv(..., stringsAsFactors=TRUE); source("analysis-gen.R", echo=TRUE); source("analysis-speecherrors.R", echo=TRUE)'
checked.result: Runs with a one-line stringsAsFactors shim (R >= 4.0). All fixed effects reproduce; SEs differ (lme4 1.1-35.5, several non-converged fits): Session p .03 -> .08; matched sleep Session x Restriction p .021 -> .085; matched sleep test p .017 -> .105. Output: reanalysis/out/authors_R_run.txt. Status present-but-insufficient because the version that produced the published SEs is not recorded.
37 participants (18 wake). One sleep participant's LIST is coded 'saf-fis' (lower case) instead of 'Saf-fis' -- harmless here.

Fails as deposited in R >= 4.0 (contr.sum on NULL levels); runs with the shim. Group beta 1.107 (SE .476, p .020) vs published 1.11 (.53, .038); OK-item intercepts reproduce (sleep z 2.56, wake 0.61).

relations.why: Item 4 of mark's blinded known-answer control of the reading protocol.

open_questions: Unblinding (mark, known_answer_control): sound or not by the third party's standard? My call before unblinding: point estimates reproduce, but two tables carry clear errors (Table 1 SDs rotated, Table 2 SEs as SDs), several p-values do not reproduce in current lme4, the SWS p-value is pseudoreplicated, and the headline effect shrinks from p < .001 to p = .039 under ANCOVA. Checked-type defects: moderate.
Which lme4 version produced the published SEs? Rerunning the deposit under lme4 ~1.1-6 (2014) would separate 'version-dependent' from 'never reproducible'.
